newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-BRITISH RUNNERS SWEEP CHICAGO MARATHON. [CORRECTED 21/10 00:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BRITISH RUNNERS SWEEP CHICAGO MARATHON. [CORRECTED 21/10 00:05 GMT]

text.p: Britons Paul Evans and Marian Sutton swept the men's and women's titles on Sunday in the 19th running of the Chicago Marathon.

Evans, a late entry who was second in the New York City Marathon last year, posted a winning time of two hours, eight minutes, 52 seconds (corrects from 51 seconds) -- the fastest Chicago time in 10 years.
Sutton, left off the British Olympic team this summer, asserted herself with a late charge to victory with a career-best time of 2:30:41.
Evans and Sutton each won $40,000 plus time bonus money.
"I've always said to myself I could run a 2:08, and now I've done it," said Evans, who also set a personal best time.

Evans broke from the field at the 18-mile mark and finished comfortably ahead of American Jerry Lawson, who clocked 2:10:04 (corrects from 2:10:03). Russian Leonid Shvetsov was third and defending champion Eamonn Martin of Britain finished fourth.

Finland's Ritva Lemettinen, bidding to become Chicago's first three-time winner, was never a threat to Sutton. She struggled home ninth and was 13 minutes slower than her winning time of a year ago. She also triumphed here in 1993.

Sutton, angered by the Olympic snub, chased American Kristy Johnston most of the way. Johnston led from the 11th mile to the 25th. At the 21st mile, Sutton learned she was 40 seconds behind and started to close the gap. She took charge with a mile to go.
"I heard she was 40 seconds behind, then 30, then 20, then 10," said Johnston. "Then I was dead meat. When she passed me I felt I had a big brick on my back."
Sutton said: "I was very upset by the British selection for the Olympics. I was unjustly left off the team. I had a point to prove today, and I think I've done that."
